sets.title: A map of Maple Street
sets.summary: Students name places on a neighborhood map, give walking directions with direction words, and argue for the best place for a new crosswalk using evidence from the map.

tasks.prompt: Look at the map of Maple Street. Name the places you see on the map.
tasks.support: Words: map, street, school, park, store, houses.

visual.alt: A neighborhood map of Maple Street with a school, a park, a store and a row of houses

models.text: School. Park. Store.
models.note: Discourse: a short list. Sentence: no sentences yet. Word: names three places with common nouns.

models.text: I see the school and the park. The store is near the houses. There is a street in the middle.
models.note: Discourse: names places and adds where some are. Sentence: simple correct sentences with I see and There is. Word: uses place words near and in the middle.

models.text: On the map, Maple Street runs through the middle of the neighborhood. The school is on one side, the park is right next to it, and the store sits on the corner across from the row of houses.
models.note: Discourse: describes the map in an organized way, from the street outward. Sentence: a long sentence that lists places in a series. Word: precise location phrases like right next to and across from.

checklist: I named places on the map.
I said where some places are.
I used words like near or next to.

tasks.prompt: A new student needs to walk from the school to the store. Tell the student how to get there. Use direction words.
tasks.support: Use: turn left, turn right, east, west, walk past, cross, across from.

visual.alt: The Maple Street map with a compass rose, showing the school on the west side and the store on the east corner

models.text: Go out school. Left. Walk park. Store there.
models.note: Discourse: steps in order. Sentence: short commands without small words like of and the. Word: uses left and the names of places.

models.text: First you go out of the school and turn left. You walk past the park. Then you cross the street and the store is in the corner. It is at east of the park.
models.note: Discourse: clear steps with first and then. Sentence: complete sentences with some errors in small words (in the corner, at east). Word: uses walk past, cross and east.

models.text: When you leave the front door of the school, turn left and walk east along Maple Street. You will pass the park on your right. At the corner, cross at the crosswalk, and the store will be directly in front of you, across from the row of houses.
models.note: Discourse: complete directions with landmarks to check the way. Sentence: uses when and will to give future steps. Word: exact direction words like east, on your right and directly in front of.

checklist: I told the steps in order.
I used direction words.
I named places to help the student find the way.

tasks.prompt: The town wants to paint one new crosswalk on Maple Street. Should it go near the school or near the store? Choose one place and explain your reasons using the map.
tasks.support: The crosswalk should go ___ because ___. On the map, ___. This would help ___.

visual.alt: The Maple Street map with people crossing the street near the school and near the store

models.text: School. Kids walk. Safe.
models.note: Discourse: a choice and one reason. Sentence: short phrases. Word: the key word safe carries the reason.

models.text: I think near the school is better. Because many kids walk there in the morning and the cars go fast. The store have less people, so it is not so important.
models.note: Discourse: a choice, a reason and a comparison with the other place. Sentence: connects ideas with because and so, with some errors (have, stand-alone because). Word: uses everyday words like less people.

models.text: I think the new crosswalk should go near the school. The map shows the school and the park are next to each other, so many children cross Maple Street there before and after school. Children are smaller and harder for drivers to see, so they need the safest place to cross. The store also gets visitors, but they come at different times of the day, so the street there is less crowded.
models.note: Discourse: claim, evidence from the map, a reason, and a fair look at the other choice. Sentence: varied sentences joined with so and but. Word: precise phrases like the map shows, safest and less crowded.

checklist: I chose one place.
I used details from the map.
I explained why it is safer.
I talked about the other place too.

sets.title: Our field trip vote
sets.summary: Students read a bar graph of class votes, compare amounts and explain how they found the difference, and judge two classmates' claims about what most students want, using numbers as evidence.

tasks.prompt: Look at the bar graph. It shows how 25 students voted for a field trip. Name the three places. Which bar is the tallest?
tasks.support: Words: graph, bar, tallest, votes, science museum, aquarium, farm.

visual.alt: A bar graph of 25 votes: science museum 11 votes, aquarium 8 votes, farm 6 votes

models.text: Museum. Fish. Farm. Museum big.
models.note: Discourse: names the places and answers the question. Sentence: words and one short phrase. Word: says fish for aquarium and big for tallest.

models.text: The places is the science museum, the aquarium and the farm. The museum bar is the tallest.
models.note: Discourse: answers both questions. Sentence: two sentences, one with an agreement error (places is). Word: uses tallest and the correct names.

models.text: The graph shows votes for the science museum, the aquarium and the farm. The science museum bar is the tallest, with 11 votes, so it got the most votes.
models.note: Discourse: names the places, answers, and adds the number as proof. Sentence: correct sentences joined with so. Word: math words like votes, the most and the exact number.

checklist: I named the three places.
I said which bar is tallest.
I used a number from the graph.

tasks.prompt: How many more students voted for the science museum than for the farm? Tell your answer and explain how you figured it out.
tasks.support: Use: more than, fewer than, difference, subtract, equals.

visual.alt: The bar graph with the science museum bar at 11 and the farm bar at 6

models.text: Museum 11. Farm 6. Five more.
models.note: Discourse: gives the two numbers and the answer. Sentence: phrases without verbs. Word: number words and more.

models.text: The museum have 11 votes and the farm have 6 votes. I take away 6 from 11 and it is 5. So 5 more students like the museum.
models.note: Discourse: the numbers, the step and the answer in order. Sentence: complete sentences with and and so, with verb errors (have). Word: uses take away instead of subtract.

models.text: Five more students voted for the science museum than for the farm. I found the difference by subtracting: the museum has 11 votes and the farm has 6, and 11 minus 6 equals 5. I can also see it on the graph, because the museum bar is 5 spaces taller than the farm bar.
models.note: Discourse: answer first, then the method, then a second way to check. Sentence: uses by and because to explain how. Word: precise math words like difference, subtracting and equals.

checklist: I gave the answer.
I explained how I found it.
I used math words like subtract or difference.

tasks.prompt: Tomás says, "Most students want to go to the science museum." Ravi says, "That is not true. More than half of the class did not vote for the museum." Who is right? Use the numbers on the graph to explain your thinking.
tasks.support: ___ is right because ___. The graph shows ___. Half of 25 is ___.

visual.alt: The bar graph of 25 votes and two students, Tomás and Ravi, with different ideas

models.text: Ravi. Museum 11. Other 14.
models.note: Discourse: picks a side and gives numbers. Sentence: words and numbers only. Word: other stands for the two other places.

models.text: I think Ravi is right. The museum has 11 votes but the aquarium and the farm together is 14 votes. 14 is more than 11, so it is not most students. But the museum still win because it has the most.
models.note: Discourse: position, evidence and an extra point about the winner. Sentence: uses but and so, with errors (together is, win). Word: uses together and the most.

models.text: Ravi is right that most students did not choose the museum. There are 25 votes in all, and half of 25 is twelve and a half. The museum got 11 votes, which is less than half, while 14 students voted for the aquarium or the farm. However, the museum still got more votes than any other single place. So the class could go there, but it is not true that most students wanted it.
models.note: Discourse: a claim, step-by-step evidence and a careful point that both students have part of the idea. Sentence: uses which, while and however to connect complex ideas. Word: precise terms like in all, less than half and any other single place.

checklist: I said who is right.
I used numbers from the graph.
I explained what half of the class means.
I used words like but or however.

sets.title: The kite in the tree
sets.summary: Students describe a story picture, retell a short story in order with time words, and explain how the main character's feelings change using details from the pictures.

tasks.prompt: Look at this picture from a story. Tell me who you see and what is happening.
tasks.support: Words: girl, grandpa, kite, tree, wind, park.

visual.alt: A girl and her grandfather in a park on a windy day, with a red kite stuck in a tall tree

models.text: Kite. Tree. Wind.
models.note: Discourse: a list of single words. Sentence: no sentences yet. Word: three nouns from the picture.

models.text: I see a girl and her grandpa. The kite is in the tree. It is windy.
models.note: Discourse: names the people and the problem. Sentence: simple correct sentences. Word: uses windy to describe the weather.

models.text: I see a girl and her grandfather standing in a park on a windy day. Their red kite is stuck high in the branches of a tree, and the girl looks worried.
models.note: Discourse: introduces the characters, the setting and the problem like the start of a story. Sentence: longer sentences with details. Word: precise words like stuck, branches and worried.

checklist: I said who is in the picture.
I said what is happening.
I used describing words.

tasks.prompt: These three pictures tell a story about Lucía and her kite. Tell the story in order: what happened first, next and last.
tasks.support: Use: first, then, suddenly, after that, finally.

visual.alt: Picture 1: Lucía and her grandpa fly a kite on a windy day. Picture 2: A strong wind blows the kite into a tree. Picture 3: A neighbor helps get the kite down, and Lucía smiles.

models.text: Kite fly. Wind. Tree. Man help.
models.note: Discourse: names each picture in order. Sentence: phrases without past tense. Word: everyday words like man for neighbor.

models.text: First Lucía and her grandpa was flying the kite. Then the wind blow very strong and the kite go in the tree. After that a neighbor come and help them. Finally Lucía was happy.
models.note: Discourse: a full beginning, middle and end with time words. Sentence: complete sentences, but past tense is not steady (was flying with they, blow, go, come). Word: uses neighbor and finally.

models.text: At first, Lucía and her grandpa were flying her kite high above the park. Suddenly, a strong gust of wind pulled the string out of her hand, and the kite got tangled in a tall tree. After that, a neighbor saw what happened and used a long pole to gently free it. Finally, Lucía got her kite back and thanked him with a huge smile.
models.note: Discourse: a story with a problem, a turning point and a solution. Sentence: correct past tense and time words like suddenly to build interest. Word: vivid words like gust, tangled and gently.

checklist: I told the story in order.
I used time words like first and then.
I talked about the past, using words like was and helped.

tasks.prompt: How did Lucía feel when her kite got stuck? How did her feelings change by the end of the story? Explain, using details from the pictures.
tasks.support: At first Lucía felt ___ because ___. Later she felt ___ when ___. This shows ___.

visual.alt: Lucía looking up sadly at the kite in the tree, and later smiling with her kite

models.text: Sad. Kite tree. Then happy.
models.note: Discourse: names two feelings in order. Sentence: words and short phrases. Word: basic feeling words sad and happy.

models.text: At first Lucía felt sad because her kite was stuck in the tree and she can't get it. Then she was happy when the neighbor help her. She smile in the last picture.
models.note: Discourse: tells how feelings change and gives reasons. Sentence: uses because and when, with errors (can't, help, smile). Word: uses the picture as evidence.

models.text: At first, Lucía probably felt worried and frustrated, because her kite was stuck so high that she and her grandpa could not reach it. In the second picture, she is looking up at the tree with a frown. By the end, her feelings changed to relief and thankfulness, since a neighbor helped her without being asked. Her smile in the last picture shows that a small act of kindness can turn a bad day around.
models.note: Discourse: traces the change from start to end and states a big idea. Sentence: uses because, since and so high that to show reasons. Word: precise feeling words like frustrated, relief and thankfulness.

checklist: I told how Lucía felt at first.
I told how her feelings changed.
I used details from the pictures.
I used because or when.
